summary: End-to-end latency spikes and intermittent request timeouts traced to function-proxy handshake during function/tool calls
description:
Issue summary:
Customer NovaHealth reports sudden increases in end-to-end inference latency and intermittent 504/timeout responses for endpoints that use tool/function calling. The spikes started on 2026-03-09 ~08:30 UTC and correlate strongly with requests that include function/tool invocation payloads (tool metadata + example calls).

Impact:
- Multiple production endpoints for NovaHealth seeing p95 latency increase from ~220ms to 850-1,200ms for requests that trigger tool calls.
- Intermittent 504s when end-to-end processing exceeds request timeout (customer and platform).
- Affects user-facing features in the NovaHealth patient triage flow (real customer impact).

Environment:
- Dedicated tenant on us-east-1, reserved GPU pool (dedicated).
- Requests use function/tool calling (function payloads include JSON schemas and examples).
- Model variants: redwood-v1-large pinned for the customer; fallback to gptj-13b observed during scale events.

Steps to reproduce (customer-provided):
1. Invoke /v1/generate with tool call enabled and include schema definitions (~2.5-6KB payload).
2. Observe streaming/chunked responses; some requests complete but with high latency, others time out.
3. When removing the schema block, median latency returns to baseline.

Observed behavior:
- Extra synchronous round-trip to function-proxy + schema-validator occurs before model tokens are emitted.
- For payloads >3KB this validation round-trip adds ~200-700ms depending on network path and proxy load.
- Under load, the function-proxy occasionally queues validation requests leading to 5xxs or timeouts upstream.

Expected behavior:
- Tool/function validation should not add a consistent blocking 200-700ms penalty to token generation.
- System should prefer async validation or overlap validation with model token emission where possible.

Temporary workaround suggested to customer:
- Disable server-side schema validation for their tenant (config flag) or reduce schema payload sizes.
- Pin to a model variant and toggle a lower validation strictness while we investigate.

Notes:
- Customer provided request IDs and timestamps; attached in comments.
investigation_notes:
Timeline & telemetry:
- 2026-03-09 08:37 UTC: multiple customer-sent traces show an additional span named function-proxy:validate_schema between api-gateway and serving-runtime.
- Baseline p95 token generation before incident: ~220ms. During incidents: p95 for same endpoints 850-1,200ms.
- Trace snippet (example trace id: 2f1e7a8b): function-proxy:validate_schema median 320ms, max 780ms; downstream model start-of-stream delayed until after validation span.
Hypotheses considered:
1) Schema validator service introduced synchronous validation call in front of token emission (regression deployed 2026-03-08).
2) Function-proxy scaling misconfiguration causing queueing under bursts for dedicated pools.
3) Network path (VPC peering for dedicated tenant) occasionally has higher latency impacting the round-trip for validation.
What we've checked so far:
- Verified PR history: serving-runtime PR #288 added an optional pre-emit schema validation call that defaults to on for tenants on dedicated plan (see related_github_prs).
- Queried function-proxy metrics: concurrent validation requests spiked at incident time; validation worker pool exhausted for short windows.
- Confirmed that disabling validation per-tenant reduces end-to-end p95 to baseline in controlled test.
Initial mitigations performed (2026-03-10):
- Temporarily disabled strict validation for NovaHealth (config flag) and validated customer reports improved latency.
- Increased validation worker pool for function-proxy in us-east-1 to reduce queuing.
Next steps:
- Engineering to triage PR that introduced synchronous validation (owner: @karim). Proposal: make validation async-by-default or stream-first-validate-later strategy.
- Add runtime feature flag to allow per-tenant async validation and document the tradeoffs.
- Add instrumentation to ensure validation span is included in SLO accounting and surface to console.
- Confirm rollout plan with SRE for controlled enablement after fix and metrics thresholding.

2026-03-11 | Karim Patel (Eng - serving-runtime): Identified PR that added pre-emit validation. Opening an internal PR to make this opt-in/async and add tests to avoid blocking emission. Linked PR: github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/322 (see related_github_prs).
2026-03-12 | Liam O'Neill (SRE): Planning a canary of async validation behavior in staging then deploy to us-east-1. Will update SLA and timeline to customer after canary results.
resolution: Investigating; temporary tenant-level validation-disable implemented as workaround. Engineering patch PR to make validation async-by-default under review. Will coordinate canary and full rollout with SRE and update customer on timeline.
next_steps: 1) Merge async-validation PR after code review and unit/integration tests. 2) Run staged canary in us-east-1 with NovaHealth traffic mirrored. 3) Re-enable tenant-level strict validation as opt-in post-rollout and communicate compliance implications. 4) Update runbook to include validation worker scaling alerts.
